source.snippet: OpenRouter notified users: 'A security researcher placed unique test URLs in prompts sent to MiniMax models from July to October 2026. A third party accessed those URLs 40 to 130 hours after the requests were sent, whether MiniMax served a request directly or another provider forwarded it to MiniMax.' — 21 points, confirmed exfiltration of prompt contents routed through an LLM aggregator to an underlying model provider.

problem_statement: Enterprises and developers routing sensitive LLM prompts through multi-provider aggregators (e.g. OpenRouter) have no reliable way to verify that underlying model providers are not reading or exfiltrating prompt contents, creating compliance and data-security risk for any business sending confidential data to AI APIs.
target_segment: Security-conscious engineering teams and compliance officers at mid-market and enterprise companies using third-party LLM API aggregators for production workloads.
notes: Confirmed real security incident with 21 HN points. Clear enterprise buyer: companies already paying for LLM API access (OpenRouter charges per token) would pay for an auditing/proxy layer that detects or prevents prompt exfiltration. Willingness-to-pay evidence: they are already spending on LLM APIs; compliance risk creates budget justification. Opportunity: a prompt-inspection proxy or audit service that sits between the client and the aggregator, flagging or redacting sensitive data and logging third-party model access patterns.
